content.text:
View A contains a yellow circle at the upper location that dominates attention and is the most immediately available; its content is moderately recoverable now and declines over two steps. The other three locations hold a blue cross at right, a red square at lower, and a green triangle at left; these are currently unattended and much less available, with lower recoverability that falls with further steps. Predicted effects of different commands show little control over A: virtually every command leaves attention on the upper location, so redirecting attention is unlikely to make other objects much more available.

View B contains a blue circle at left that currently dominates attention and is immediately available; a green cross at lower is unattended but has relatively high recoverability; a red square at upper and a yellow triangle at right are both unattended with modest recoverability. Predicted command effects for B are strongly controllable: issuing a command named for a location shifts predicted attention to that location, making that location become the primary, highly available object while the others lose availability.
